---
title: "Dwell Time"
description: "How long readers stay on each Signal Check edition and dashboard, as a drop-off curve of page views."
---

How long readers keep a Signal Check edition or a published dashboard open
and visible, measured per page from the meta-analytics GA4 property.

Dwell time is a drop-off curve, not a single average. Each page fires one
event the first time a page view reaches 1, 5, 15, 30, 60, 120, 300, and 600
seconds of visible time (`read_1s` through `read_600s`). The share of page
views that reached each mark shows how far readers get. The median reader's
dwell time is read off that curve.

Only Signal Check editions and the dashboards fire these events. The Metrics
Cookbook stream does not, nor does any production CanadaLogin page.

## Calculation

Dwell curve: for each page and each milestone, divide the `read_Ns` event
count by the `page_view` event count over the reporting window. Both come from
[`meta_page_events`](../../catalog/google_analytics/meta_page_events.qmd).

Median dwell time: the time at which half of the page's views were still open.
Take the last milestone at least half the views reached and the next one, and
interpolate on a log scale to where the share crosses 50%. It is 0 when fewer
than half reached 1 second, and infinite when half were still open at 600
seconds.

Group on `pagepath_redacted`, never `pagepath`, which holds a private token
for Signal Check pages.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Example queries"}

::: {.panel-tabset}

## SQL

Dwell curve:

```sql
WITH events AS (
    SELECT
        pagepath_redacted,
        eventname,
        SUM(eventcount) AS n
    FROM google_analytics.meta_page_events
    WHERE page_kind IN ('signal_check', 'dashboard')
      AND (eventname = 'page_view' OR REGEXP_LIKE(eventname, '^read_[0-9]+s$'))
      -- set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
      AND CAST(date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-01' AND DATE '2026-09-30'
    GROUP BY pagepath_redacted, eventname
),
views AS (
    SELECT pagepath_redacted, n AS page_views
    FROM events
    WHERE eventname = 'page_view'
)
SELECT
    e.pagepath_redacted,
    CAST(REGEXP_EXTRACT(e.eventname, '[0-9]+') AS INTEGER) AS milestone_seconds,
    v.page_views,
    e.n AS page_views_reached,
    CAST(e.n AS DOUBLE) / v.page_views AS share_reached
FROM events e
JOIN views v ON e.pagepath_redacted = v.pagepath_redacted
WHERE e.eventname <> 'page_view'
ORDER BY e.pagepath_redacted, milestone_seconds;
```

Median dwell time:

```sql
WITH events AS (
    SELECT
        pagepath_redacted,
        eventname,
        SUM(eventcount) AS n
    FROM google_analytics.meta_page_events
    WHERE page_kind IN ('signal_check', 'dashboard')
      AND (eventname = 'page_view' OR REGEXP_LIKE(eventname, '^read_[0-9]+s$'))
      -- set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
      AND CAST(date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-01' AND DATE '2026-09-30'
    GROUP BY pagepath_redacted, eventname
),
views AS (
    SELECT pagepath_redacted, n AS page_views
    FROM events
    WHERE eventname = 'page_view'
),
-- every milestone, so one nobody reached reads as zero, not missing
curve AS (
    SELECT
        v.pagepath_redacted,
        v.page_views,
        m.seconds,
        CAST(COALESCE(e.n, 0) AS DOUBLE) / v.page_views AS share,
        LEAD(m.seconds) OVER (PARTITION BY v.pagepath_redacted ORDER BY m.seconds) AS next_seconds,
        LEAD(CAST(COALESCE(e.n, 0) AS DOUBLE) / v.page_views)
            OVER (PARTITION BY v.pagepath_redacted ORDER BY m.seconds) AS next_share
    FROM views v
    CROSS JOIN UNNEST(ARRAY[1, 5, 15, 30, 60, 120, 300, 600]) AS m (seconds)
    LEFT JOIN events e
        ON e.pagepath_redacted = v.pagepath_redacted
       AND e.eventname = 'read_' || CAST(m.seconds AS VARCHAR) || 's'
),
crossing AS (
    SELECT
        *,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY pagepath_redacted ORDER BY seconds DESC) AS rn
    FROM curve
    WHERE share >= 0.5
)
SELECT
    v.pagepath_redacted,
    v.page_views,
    CASE
        -- fewer than half of the page views reached 1 second
        WHEN c.seconds IS NULL THEN 0
        -- half were still open at the last milestone
        WHEN c.next_seconds IS NULL THEN infinity()
        ELSE exp(ln(c.seconds) + (c.share - 0.5) / (c.share - c.next_share)
                 * (ln(c.next_seconds) - ln(c.seconds)))
    END AS median_dwell_seconds
FROM views v
LEFT JOIN crossing c
    ON c.pagepath_redacted = v.pagepath_redacted
   AND c.rn = 1
ORDER BY v.pagepath_redacted;
```

## R

Dwell curve:

```r
events <- tbl(con, in_schema("google_analytics", "meta_page_events")) |>
  filter(
    page_kind %in% c("signal_check", "dashboard"),
    eventname == "page_view" | str_detect(eventname, "^read_[0-9]+s$"),
    # set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
    as.Date(date) >= as.Date("2026-09-01"),
    as.Date(date) <= as.Date("2026-09-30")
  ) |>
  group_by(pagepath_redacted, eventname) |>
  summarise(n = sum(eventcount, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

views <- events |>
  filter(eventname == "page_view") |>
  select(pagepath_redacted, page_views = n)

events |>
  filter(eventname != "page_view") |>
  inner_join(views, by = "pagepath_redacted") |>
  transmute(
    pagepath_redacted,
    milestone_seconds = as.integer(str_extract(eventname, "[0-9]+")),
    page_views,
    page_views_reached = n,
    share_reached = as.numeric(n) / page_views
  ) |>
  arrange(pagepath_redacted, milestone_seconds)
```

Median dwell time:

```r
milestones <- c(1, 5, 15, 30, 60, 120, 300, 600)

# The time half the page views were still open, interpolated on a log scale
# between the milestones either side of 50%. `seconds` must be sorted.
median_read <- function(seconds, share) {
  above <- which(share >= 0.5)
  if (length(above) == 0L) return(0)
  i <- max(above)
  if (i == length(seconds)) return(Inf)
  step <- (share[i] - 0.5) / (share[i] - share[i + 1L])
  exp(log(seconds[i]) + step * (log(seconds[i + 1L]) - log(seconds[i])))
}

events <- tbl(con, in_schema("google_analytics", "meta_page_events")) |>
  filter(
    page_kind %in% c("signal_check", "dashboard"),
    eventname == "page_view" | str_detect(eventname, "^read_[0-9]+s$"),
    # set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
    as.Date(date) >= as.Date("2026-09-01"),
    as.Date(date) <= as.Date("2026-09-30")
  ) |>
  group_by(pagepath_redacted, eventname) |>
  summarise(n = sum(eventcount, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  collect() |>
  mutate(n = as.numeric(n))

views <- events |>
  filter(eventname == "page_view") |>
  select(pagepath_redacted, page_views = n)

reached <- events |>
  filter(eventname != "page_view") |>
  transmute(
    pagepath_redacted,
    seconds = as.numeric(str_extract(eventname, "[0-9]+")),
    n
  )

views |>
  # every milestone, so one nobody reached reads as zero, not missing
  cross_join(tibble(seconds = milestones)) |>
  left_join(reached, by = c("pagepath_redacted", "seconds")) |>
  mutate(share = coalesce(n, 0) / page_views) |>
  arrange(pagepath_redacted, seconds) |>
  group_by(pagepath_redacted, page_views) |>
  summarise(median_dwell_seconds = median_read(seconds, share), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(pagepath_redacted)
```

:::

:::

## Interpretation notes

Only visible time counts. The clock pauses while the tab is in the
background and resumes when the reader comes back, so a tab left open
overnight does not reach `read_600s` unless someone is looking at it.

The median is an estimate between two measured milestones. A
`median_dwell_seconds` of 45 means half the views passed 30 seconds and fewer
than half passed 60; the interpolation places the crossing in between. An
infinite median means half the views were still open at 10 minutes, so report
it as "over 10 minutes". Signal Checks before #9 report the floor milestone
instead, the longest milestone at least half the views reached, so their
medians read lower.

Prefer the curve or the median to an average. Readership is small, often a
few dozen page views per page per month, and one forgotten tab can move a
mean a long way. At these counts, check `page_views` before comparing two
pages. A share built on five page views is too unstable to rank.

The curve counts page views, not people. A reader who reloads the page, or
comes back on another day, starts the milestones again and counts twice. Use
`page_views` as the denominator, since `totalusers` in `meta_page_events`
can't be summed across days.

`read_1s` is approximate. The page checks the clock once a second, so
`read_1s` means "1 to 2 seconds". Milestones from 15 seconds up are not
affected.

This metric covers only Signal Check editions and the dashboards. Public
CanadaLogin pages do not fire `read_Ns` events. For time on those pages, use
GA4's built-in
[average engagement time](https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/11109416),
which is only available in the GA4 interface, not in the data lake.

## Alternative names

- time on page
- reading time
- read depth
- engagement time
